core_obligations: Apply the adjunction (proof lines 4625-4628): for every complex G^bullet of O'-modules, the adjunction identifies Hom_{K(O')}(G^bullet, Hom_O(O', I^bullet)) with Hom_{K(O)}(G^bullet, I^bullet), where G^bullet is regarded as a complex of O-modules along the map O -> O'.

Conclude K-injectivity (proof line 4629): since I^bullet is K-injective over O, the right hand side vanishes whenever G^bullet is acyclic, so the left hand side does too, which is the K-injectivity of SheafHom_O(O', I^bullet) as a complex of O'-modules.
proof_roadmap: Test K-injectivity of the restricted internal hom against homotopy classes of maps from complexes of O'-modules.
Rewrite those hom groups by the adjunction as hom groups over O into the K-injective I^bullet.
Acyclicity of the test complex makes the latter vanish.
Hence the restricted internal hom is K-injective over O'.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that restricting scalars along a map O -> O' of sheaves of rings on a site turns a K-injective complex of O-modules into a K-injective complex of O'-modules when packaged as SheafHom_O(O', I^bullet) (statement lines 4615-4622). The proof is a single adjunction identification: K-injectivity is tested through homotopy classes of maps from complexes of O'-modules, and the adjunction rewrites those groups as homotopy classes of maps over O into the K-injective I^bullet, whose vanishing in the acyclic case is the hypothesis (proof lines 4625-4629). The content is the choice of the right adjunction. The claim is H2: one identification of hom groups, with the adjunction coming from another chapter.
